props.title: The Game
props.initialSlug: Wealthy banker's reality unravels in sinister game

sections.content: The Game stands as David Fincher's most underappreciated masterpiece, coming between his breakout Se7en (1995) and Fight Club (1999). Michael Douglas delivers a career-defining performance as Nicholas Van Orton, a wealthy investment banker whose controlled world unravels through an elaborate "game" that blurs reality and fiction. The film masterfully builds paranoia through calculated set pieces, joining other psychological thrillers of the late 90s like Dark City (1998) and eXistenZ (1999) in questioning the nature of reality itself.

sections.content: Fincher's meticulous direction in The Game established techniques he'd perfect in later works like Zodiac (2007) and Gone Girl (2014). The film's exploration of wealthy isolation echoes similar themes in American Psycho (2000) and Eyes Wide Shut (1999), where privileged protagonists face psychological breakdowns that challenge their perceived control over reality.

The film's influence appears in later reality-bending thrillers like Inception (2010) and Shutter Island (2010), where protagonists question everything they experience. The "game within reality" concept inspired Ready or Not (2019) and Escape Room (2019), though none match Fincher's sophisticated execution. SUBHEAD: The Art of Paranoid Cinema

movies.title: Mulholland Drive
movies.slug: A surreal psychological thriller about an aspiring actress in Los Angeles whose reality begins to fracture

sections.content: The Game perfects the paranoid thriller format established by classics like The Manchurian Candidate (1962) and Three Days of the Condor (1975). Its innovative structure influenced modern mind-benders like Source Code (2011) and Vanilla Sky (2001), where reality becomes increasingly unstable as the narrative progresses. The film's San Francisco setting becomes a character itself, much like in Fincher's later Zodiac (2007), with the city's steep streets and gothic architecture amplifying the protagonist's descent into chaos.
